title: Deep learning scores non-coding variants in congenital heart disease
summary: Single-cell chromatin accessibility maps of human fetal heart were generated, and deep learning models predicting cell-type-resolved, base-resolution accessibility from DNA sequence were interpreted to infer motif lexicons and score non-coding variants. De novo mutations predicted to affect accessibility in arterial endothelium were enriched in congenital heart disease cases versus controls, and CRISPR perturbation validated one enhancer harboring a nominated mutation, linking it to JARID2 expression. Validation covers a single enhancer. Preprint of 2022-06-29.
ai_technology: Deep learning models predicting cell-type-resolved chromatin accessibility profiles from DNA sequence, used to score non-coding variants

evidence.tested: CRISPR-based perturbation of one nominated regulatory enhancer; case-control enrichment of predicted variant effects.
evidence.unknown: Causality of other nominated variants is not established; abstract-level review; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning models scored non-coding de novo variants for regulatory effect.
